item.title: Crypto’s Push Into Wall Street Suffers Setback After Bill Fails
item.description: Crypto’s long march into mainstream finance took a step backward Tuesday when the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act, denying the industry a chance to turn its newfound influence in Washington into fresh rules that could outlast the current administration.
item.dc:creator: Olga Kharif and Scott Patterson

item.title: Senate Advances Legislation to Regulate College Sports Landscape
item.description: The Senate advanced a bipartisan bill that would attempt to regulate the rapidly-changing world of college sports, in a rush to move the legislation before lawmakers leave Washington for the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Janet Lorin and Steven T. Dennis

item.title: Businessweek Daily: Future Proof Day Special (Podcast)
item.description:
Wall Street traders refrained from making riskier bets in the countdown to the Federal Reserve decision, with stocks falling as elevated oil prices drove bond yields to multi-year highs. Almost 350 firms in the S&P 500 dropped. Benchmark 10-year yields hit the highest level in nearly two decades. Longer-dated Treasuries extended losses after a weak $13 billion sale of 20-year bonds. Brent crude settled above $108, fueling inflation worries. Bitcoin tumbled as the US Senate blocked a landmark crypto bill in an industry loss.
On today's episode Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec host from a special episode in Huntington Beach, CA:
Tony Davidow, Senior Private Market Strategist, Franklin Templeton Institute Jan van Eck, VanEck Funds CEO Jaime Magyera, Senior Managing Director, Head of U.S. Wealth and Head of Retirement, BlackRock Scott Dennis, Head of ETFs, TCW (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump's Midterm Mail Ballot Curbs
item.description: The US Supreme Court refused to clear the Postal Service to enforce new restrictions on mail-in ballots for the congressional midterms, in a rebuff to the Trump administration. Jeff Mason has more on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Iran War Blockade Costs Strain Taiwan China Deterrence
item.description: The cost of naval operations since the buildup began in January has topped $7.1 billion — not including all the US assets being used to escort tankers through the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Gerry Doyle, Becca Wasser, Jen Judson, Courtney McBride and Hayley Warren

item.title: Bond Yields Surge Ahead of the Fed Rate Decision
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are DWS Group Head of Fixed Income, Americas George Catrambone, Upwork CEO Hayden Brown, Citizens Equity Research Analyst, Managing Director Jay McCanless, VSORA Chair Sandra Rivera, Rockefeller Global Family Office Private Advisor Angela Mwanza, Oaktree Portfolio Manager Danielle Poli, Wellington Management Private Capital Formation & Investor Relations Head Laura Kirk, Robinhood Futures & Prediction Markets VP & GM JB Mackenzie, MoneyGram CEO Anthony Soohoo, & Dutch Bros CEO & President Christine Barone. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Angela Mwanza Sees 25-Basis-Point Fed Cut
item.description: Angela Mwanza, Managing Director and Private Advisor at Rockefeller Global Family Office, joined the program to discuss the Federal Reserve outlook ahead of tomorrow’s decision. In response to whether the Fed will act, she said she thinks the central bank is looking at a 25-basis-point move. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Bailey Lipschultz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sheinbaum Tax Change Eyes New Revenue But Businesses Fear Impact
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum is proposing sweeping changes to corporate income tax rules to raise as much as 140 billion pesos ($8.2 billion) next year, part of an effort to narrow the budget deficit but one that risks squeezing low-margin businesses.
item.dc:creator: Alex Vasquez and Gonzalo Soto

item.title: Robinhood Predictions VP on Growth in Event Contracts
item.description: JB Mackenzie, Robinhood Futures & Prediction Markets VP & GM, discusses rising trading activity in prediction markets ahead of the Federal Reserve’s rate decision, with markets pricing in an roughly 85% chance of a 25-basis-point hike. He sas interest in Fed-related contracts has grown substantially over the past year, moving from relatively muted early adoption to one of Robinhood’s most popular contracts. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Leon Black Contempt Resolution Advanced by House Epstein Panel
item.description: The House committee investigating disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein voted to recommend holding billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress Tuesday after he defied subpoenas for testimony and documents related to women in Epstein’s orbit.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly

item.title: Canada Is a Sleeping Giant Economically, Says Blackstone's Gray
item.description: Blackstone Inc. President Jon Gray says Canada has massive opportunities to grow due to its natural resources, looser regulatory policies and access to private capital. “Canada is a sleeping giant economically," he said Tuesday at an investment summit in Toronto. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investors Contend With AI Alarms, Global Risk at Future Proof
item.description:
Paisley Nardini, Head of Investment Strategy for Tema ETFs, discusses the industry group ETFs that are surging right now as industry leaders gather in Huntington Beach, California for Future Proof. Then, Hamilton Reiner, Portfolio Manager and CIO for the US Core Equity Team at JPMorgan Asset Management. Plus, Tony Davidow, Senior Private Market Strategist at Franklin Templeton Institute and discusses the wave of AI companies going public and the private market landscape and Chris Galipeau, Head Market Strategist at Franklin Templeton Institute, discusses the public market environment. Finally, Jan van Eck, breaks down the long term macro environment and the where he sees the AI trade going amid 'doomerism' from some skeptics. re he sees the AI trade going amid 'doomerism' from some skeptics.
Correct: Fixes JPMorgan Asset Management. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Warsh and the Fed Face Rate-Day Decision Reckoning With Markets, and Trump
item.description: Any course of action carries risks for the Fed chairman
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Trump Defends AI Amid Voter Unease
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest news from DC. On today's show, former Secretary of State Antony Blinken, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Groundwork Collaborative Senior Fellow Kitty Richards. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Stocks and Tokens Drop After Senate Blocks Landmark Bill
item.description: Senators from both parties blocked a landmark digital asset market structure bill in a procedural vote Tuesday, sending cryptocurrency stocks tumbling after a major setback for industry.
item.dc:creator: Lydia Beyoud and Steven T. Dennis

item.title: Trump Says Kennedy Center Revamp Hinges on Adding His Name
item.description: President Donald Trump threatened to scrap efforts to repair the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts unless his name is added to the building, shortly after his hand-picked board approved a renovation plan.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Merz Cancels UN Trip to Address CDU Party Rebellion in Berlin
item.description: Friedrich Merz cancelled his trip to the United Nations General Assembly in New York next week, changing course as the German chancellor faces growing opposition within his own conservative party ahead of closely-watched regional elections on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs

item.title: Brazil Top Court Puts Off Moraes Decision, Clouding Election
item.description: Brazil’s Supreme Court delayed a decision on whether to open an unprecedented investigation into one of its justices Tuesday after a tense public hearing in which members traded accusations of political bias and spreading falsehoods about each other.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho, Martha Beck and Beatriz Reis

item.title: Hong Kong Leader to Unveil Five-Year Plan That Outlasts His Term
item.description: Hong Kong leader John Lee is taking the unprecedented step of outlining a five-year vision for the Asian financial hub. The question is whether he’ll be the chief executive to see it through.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan

item.title: Pentagon Watchdog Sees Strategic Munitions Shortage
item.description: The US fired so many munitions at Iranian targets during the first few months of Operation Epic Fury that it “has resulted in strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply,” Pentagon officials acknowledged to the Defense Department’s independent watchdog.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio
